modeling_notes: The current catalog publishes its categorical course requirements inside a four-semester pathway. Reorganize those rows by requirement; semester placement is not an additional schedule requirement.
The two separate Block II slots are retained as two course selections and are resolved against the catalog's linked Block II option record.
The program prints two separate four-credit slots with the same PHY 241 or CHM 111 choice. They are retained as distinct slots and cannot reuse the same applied course credit.

The MTH 264 or MTH 245 slot is printed as four credits, while MTH 245 is a three-credit course. That one-credit choice explains the catalog's 60-61 total and is preserved rather than padded with an invented course.

data_quality_flags.message: Two distinct four-credit requirements share the identical PHY 241 or CHM 111 menu; the same course credit cannot satisfy both slots.
The MTH 264/MTH 245 row is printed as four credits, but MTH 245 carries three credits, producing the published 60-61 range.

narrative: This degree program is designed for the student preparing for transfer to a four year program in Computer Science. The student is responsible for determining transferability to a four-year college or university. This program is G3 Eligible.

This program is aligned with the Transfer Virginia Computer Science AS common curriculum. Students are strongly encouraged to consult with their academic advisor and review program options using the Transfer Virginia Portal or in consultation with their intended four-year institution.
unassigned: Satisfactory completion of the following high school units or equivalent as a minimum: 4 years of English, 3 years of mathematics (Algebra I, Algebra II, and Geometry), 1 year of laboratory science and 1 year of social science.
Students with deficiencies will require developmental studies and will not be able to complete the program within a two-year window.
All students expected to complete the requirements for a degree, diploma, certificate, or career studies certificate must complete an Application for Graduation.
